chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one performing Tamattu' who comes, fulfills his Tamattu', then a need arises for him, so he goes out to Al-Madinah, or to Dhat 'Irq, or to one of the places. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should return to Makkah with an Umrah if it is in a month other than the month in which he performed Tamattu', because for every month there is an Umrah, and he is pledged with the Hajj.'

I said: 'And if he enters during the month in which he went out?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) was residing here, so he went out to meet some of them. So when he returned, he reached Dhat 'Irq, he entered into Ihram from Dhat 'Irq for the Hajj, and entered (Makkah) while he was in Ihram for the Hajj.'

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: He entered into Ihram (state of consecration)
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.ذَاتِ عِرْقٍ: Dhat 'Irq (a place near Makkah where pilgrims enter Ihram)
key_terms.مُتْعَتَهُ: His Tamattu' (the Umrah portion of the combined pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mutamatti' pilgrer who leaves Makkah after Umrah but before Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'Iqar' (being held in pledge) for a Mutamatti', distinguishing between leaving during the Hajj month versus outside it. Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes that if one departs outside the sacred month, a fresh Umrah is required to release the Hajj obligation, whereas departing within the month allows one to assume Ihram for Hajj from the current location, such as Dhat 'Irq. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the geographical boundaries of Ihram for those combining rituals.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ishaq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the performer of Tumatto who comes over, so he fulfills his Tumatto, then the need appears for him, so he goes out to Al-Medina, or to Zaat Irq, or to one of the places. Heasws said: ‘He should return to Makkah for Umra if it was during other than the month in which he performed Tumatto in, because for every month there is an Umra, and he is pledged with the Hajj’.

I said, ‘Supposing he enters during the month in which he went out?’ Heasws said: ‘Myasws was in the vicinity over there. So heasws went out to meet some of them. So when heasws was returning, heasws reached Zaat Irq, heasws wore Ihraam from Zaat Irq for the Hajj, and entered (Makkah) and heasws was in Ihraam for the Hajj’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous). He comes and completes his Mut‘ah, then he for a certain work goes to al-Madinah or to Dhat ‘Irq or to a certain other place. He (the Imam) said, ‘He returns to Makkah for al-‘Umrah if it is in the months in which Mut‘ah is performed; for every month there is al-‘Umrah and he is bound with al-Hajj.’

I then asked, ‘What can happen if he enters in the month in which he left?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘My father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was residing here and he once went to meet certain ones of these people. When he returned and reached Dhat ‘Irq he assumed the state of Ihram for al-Hajj. He entered in the state of Ihram for al-Hajj.’”
